articles.title: Jayden Daniels Teammates' Response to Injury Addressed by Commanders HC After Viral Videos
articles.summary: When Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels suffered a gruesome elbow injury against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday, the response from his teammates was pointed out by NFL fans.
articles.body:
When Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels suffered a gruesome elbow injury against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday, the response from his teammates was pointed out by NFL fans.

While many of Daniels' teammates walked to the sideline immediately after he went down, head coach Dan Quinn said his players were torn up over the injury.

"It's just the opposite," Quinn told reporters on Wednesday. "These guys were absolutely gutted. When the half is over... I can't delay the half. They can't stay on the field. They were gutted. They love this guy."

As Quinn noted, the play where Daniels was injured occurred right as the first half ended, so players quickly had to get off the field and go into the locker room. It surely would have been a different scene if the injury had taken place at a different point in the game.

Unfortunately for the Commanders, Daniels is now likely set to miss an extended period of time, making a 0-2 start for Washington even more difficult to overcome. Daniels suffered the same injury in Week 9 last season and was able to return in Week 14.

Until Daniels returns, Marcus Mariota will take the reins on offense and try to keep the Commanders afloat.

articles.title: Chris Johnson’s heartbreaking ALS story will leave you in tears: How a strange feeling in his hand changed his life forever
articles.summary: Former NFL running back Chris Johnson has spent much of his life being defined by speed.
articles.body: Former NFL running back Chris Johnson has spent much of his life being defined by speed. He became one of the most explosive players of his generation, rushing for 2,006 yards in 2009 and finishing that season with an NFL-record 2,509 yards from scrimmage. But years after walking away from football, Johnson found himself facing a challenge no amount of athleticism could prepare him for: amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, better known as ALS.What began with an unusual feeling in his right hand in early 2025 has since progressed at a devastating pace, changing nearly every part of Johnson’s daily life.Now, at 40, Johnson is sharing more of his story, opening up about the first signs of the disease, his diagnosis, his family’s struggle, his questions about whether football could have played a role, and his determination to spend as much time as possible with his wife and four children.Chris Johnson opens up on devastating ALS battle after losing ability to speak and walk independentlyJohnson has now revealed that the first noticeable symptoms appeared in early 2025. He was working out regularly and spending time with his wife, Brittany, and their four children when he began experiencing weakness in his right hand.At first, he did not think much of it. Johnson said his grip simply did not feel right and that he wasn't as strong as he had always been. His wife initially thought the problem might be connected to the years he had spent playing football.A pinched nerve or an old football-related issue seemed more plausible than something as serious as ALS. Then came a moment during a family road trip that made Johnson realize the problem could be more significant.During spring break in March 2025, Johnson picked up his water bottle and told Brittany that it suddenly felt heavy. The bottle itself hadn't changed. His ability to hold it had.Johnson later explained that his right hand had already felt strained for several weeks, but the water bottle incident convinced him that he needed to find out what was happening.The doctor's visit that changed everythingJohnson contacted a former Titans team doctor, who helped him get a nerve-conduction study in Nashville. The test did not immediately give him a diagnosis.Instead, Johnson was given paperwork that referred to “Possible Anterior Horn Cell Disease” and was told to see another doctor because the results could be serious.It was only later, while sitting at the airport and talking to Brittany, that Johnson and his wife began researching what the terminology meant. One of the diseases associated with that category was ALS. That was the moment the possibility became real for the family.Johnson was eventually diagnosed with sporadic ALS in 2025, at age 39. Doctors told him there was no known family history of ALS in his case.How quickly ALS changed Chris Johnson's lifeThe most striking part of Johnson's story has been the speed at which his condition progressed. When he first noticed the weakness, he was still living an active life and spending time with his children. By the time he publicly revealed his diagnosis in June 2026, his physical abilities had changed dramatically.Johnson appeared on Good Morning America with Michael Strahan and communicated through a speech-generating device controlled with his eyes. His voice had been recorded after his diagnosis, allowing the device to reproduce it as he typed using eye movements.Johnson explained that the disease had progressed much faster than he ever imagined. He recalled that only a little more than a year earlier, he had been able to pick up his young daughter and help her make a wish over her birthday cake.By the time of the interview, he could no longer do that. “I want people to understand just how quickly ALS can attack your body,” Johnson said.Chris Johnson's wife Brittany becomes his primary caregiverJohnson has repeatedly emphasized that he has not gone through the disease alone.His wife, Brittany, has remained by his side throughout the diagnosis and progression of his illness.In his initial public interview, Brittany described how difficult it was to watch her husband's life change so quickly. She said the family initially hoped doctors were wrong and that the symptoms could be explained by something else.Instead, the family had to adjust to an entirely different reality. By September 2026, Brittany had become Johnson's primary caregiver.Recent reporting says she has been helping him with everyday tasks, including feeding, changing, and stretching, while Johnson also relies on breathing support from a CPAP machine.For Brittany, the disease has affected the entire family, not only the person diagnosed. Johnson has echoed that sentiment, saying ALS has changed life for everyone around him.One of the central messages Johnson has tried to communicate throughout his ALS journey is that the disease has not changed his identity.During his Good Morning America appearance, he made it clear that while ALS had taken away many of his physical abilities, his thoughts, emotions and love for his family remained.“I want people to know that I'm still me,” Johnson said. “ALS has changed what my body can do, but it hasn't changed who I am.” The same idea became even more prominent in his September 2026 letter to his children.Writing for The Players' Tribune, Johnson told his children that almost every part of his life had changed, but that he remained their father, Brittany's husband and the same person they had always known. He said his value was not determined by what his body could physically do.His children have become his biggest motivationFor Johnson, his four children are at the heart of his fight. When he first received the diagnosis, Brittany said one of her immediate thoughts was about how young their children were. Johnson has repeatedly said that his children give him a reason to continue fighting. He wants more time with them. He wants to watch them grow up, make memories with them, and simply continue being their father.In his September letter, Johnson reflected on the future he hopes to see with his children, including watching them reach major milestones in their lives. That desire has become one of the defining themes of Johnson's ALS journey.Chris Johnson wonders whether football played a roleJohnson has also begun asking a difficult question: Could his NFL career have contributed to his ALS?He has been to numerous neurologists and major ALS clinics since his diagnosis and said he noticed that doctors sometimes reacted differently after learning that he had played professional football.Johnson referenced research indicating that former NFL players were nearly four times as likely to develop and die from ALS as the overall U.S. male population. But Johnson has been careful not to claim that football caused his illness.He acknowledged that he is not a medical expert, that the research represents only one study, and that other environmental factors could be involved. His position is essentially that he cannot help wondering whether there could be a connection between his football career and his diagnosis.That distinction is important: Johnson has raised the question, not established a cause.Johnson has also chosen to fight the disease through available medical research. He has participated in experimental treatments and a clinical trial, saying that he hopes the efforts can extend his life while also contributing to greater understanding of ALS.When he first announced his diagnosis, Johnson explained that research and the work being done by doctors gave him hope. He also wanted his story to encourage earlier diagnosis and greater investment in ALS research. His family has also helped support fundraising and awareness efforts connected to ALS research.His Titans Ring of Honor ceremony was postponedJohnson's health battle has even affected one of the biggest honors of his football career. The Titans had planned to induct him into the team's Ring of Honor on September 13, 2026.But Johnson and his family were unable to travel to Nashville because of his condition, so the ceremony was postponed. The Titans instead held a halftime celebration recognizing Johnson and his career. The moment offered a striking contrast.The former running back who once electrified Nashville with his speed could no longer make the trip to receive the honor in person.Where Chris Johnson is nowAs of September 2026, Johnson's ALS has progressed to the point where he cannot speak normally and relies on an eye-controlled device to communicate. He requires significant assistance from his family for daily activities and uses CPAP support for breathing.His wife Brittany remains his primary caregiver, while their children continue to be a central source of motivation. Yet Johnson continues to communicate publicly and tell his story.In his September letter to his children, he reflected on the enormous changes ALS has brought to his life while emphasizing that the disease cannot define the entirety of who he is. His football career made him famous for his speed.His ALS journey has forced him to confront what happens when his body can no longer move the way it once did. articles.title: Jonah Coleman, JK Dobbins, RJ Harvey Injury Updates, Latest Rumors on Broncos RBs for Week 3
articles.summary: The Denver Broncos are dealing with quite a few injuries at the running back position heading into a Week 3 showdown against the Los Angeles Rams.
articles.body:
The Denver Broncos are dealing with quite a few injuries at the running back position heading into a Week 3 showdown against the Los Angeles Rams.

Per ESPN's Adam Schefter , "Jonah Coleman is dealing with a sprained ankle that he suffered in Sunday's game vs. Jacksonville, per source. Denver running back RJ Harvey continues to make progress on his hamstring recovery, and the team also received good news on running back JK Dobbins, who left Sunday's game early, but is expected to practice this week."

Dobbins, 27, has led the backfield thus far, rushing 18 times for 72 yards. That was the expectation coming into the season, with the veteran bruiser the team's preferred option between the tackles.

Underperforming Players With the Most to Prove 🏈

Harvey, 25, operated as the lightning to Dobbins' thunder last season, though a hamstring injury kept him out of action in Week 2 and has called into question his availability for Week 3.

"I think there's a lot ahead of us this week in regards to who our runners are going to be," head coach Sean Payton acknowledged while speaking to reporters on Monday.

The 23-year-old Coleman, a rookie, operated in a complementary role to Dobbins on Sunday, rushing 10 times for 39 yards and a touchdown while also catching three passes for 19 yards.

"J.K. always preaches to me, be ready for your opportunity, be ready for your moment, you never know when your number is going to be called," Coleman told reporters after Sunday's 2013 win over the Jacksonville Jaguars. "... It felt good to be able to do that."

From a fantasy football perspective, there remains plenty of uncertainty regarding who will be available on Sunday night, though it sounds as though Dobbins is a safe bet. All three players should absolutely be rostered in all formats, though none are anything more than flex considerations against a tough L.A. defensive line.

articles.title: Matthew Stafford's Wife Kelly Treating Season Like 'It's the Last' for Rams QB amid Retirement Buzz
articles.summary: The wife of Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford is approaching his NFL career with a year-by-year mindset.
articles.body:
The wife of Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford is approaching his NFL career with a year-by-year mindset.

"Every season now I will say I'm treating it like the last," Kelly Stafford said to People 's Skyler Caruso . "It's been 18 years now. It's been a wild, wild ride."

Kelly made it clear she has no idea when her husband with actually hang it up. Assuming 2026 could be his final year helps her appreciate each game as it comes.

"The feeling of taking the girls to the game and watching their dad run over, that fills my soul with so much joy," she said. "I'm going to completely miss it when it's gone so much, but I also have to prepare for that moment.

"Treating this season like it's the last of everything. That's how I'm looking at it right now."

Matthew Stafford is under contract through 2028, but he and the Rams restructured his deal in a way that eases the salary cap implications if he retires before that.

Los Angeles has already lined up a succession plan. It wouldn't have used a first-round draft pick on Ty Simpson if it felt confident about Stafford playing for another four or five years.

The Rams' first two games haven't provided any added insight into what the 38-year-old will decide about his playing status for 2027. He and the team rebounded from a Week 1 loss to the San Francisco 49ers by beating the New York Giants 28-6. Stafford went 22-of-31 for 327 yards, four touchdowns and one interception.

In Week 1, Stafford showed his age a bit. But if his Week 2 performance is more indicative of what's to come, he may have a hard time walking away when he clearly has a lot left in the tank.

articles.title: Giants QB Jaxson Dart is expected to have season-ending knee surgery
articles.summary: New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart is expected to have season-ending surgery on his left knee, according to a person with knowledge of the details of the injury.
articles.body: New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart is expected to have season-ending surgery on his left knee, according to a person with knowledge of the details of the injury. The person spoke to The Associated Press on condition of anonymity Wednesday because the team has not announced Dart’s status. Dart was injured on the first drive Monday night against the Los Angeles Rams when his left leg bent awkwardly as he was hit by two defenders. After initially saying it was in the neighborhood of a medial collateral ligament injury, coach John Harbaugh said Tuesday the evaluation process for Dart was still ongoing. articles.title: Lawyer: Ex-NFL Star Antonio Brown to Avoid Prison with Reduced Charge in Attempted Murder Case
articles.summary: Former NFL star wide receiver Antonio Brown plans to accept a plea deal that will have him avoid prison time on a reduced charge in an attempted murder case in Miami. His lawyer said Wednesday the agreement with prosecutors was too good to turn down.
articles.body:
Former NFL star wide receiver Antonio Brown plans to accept a plea deal that will have him avoid prison time on a reduced charge in an attempted murder case in Miami. His lawyer said Wednesday the agreement with prosecutors was too good to turn down.

Brown is scheduled to appear in court on Sept. 30 to make the deal final. Defense attorney Mark Eiglarsh said Brown will plead no contest to aggravated assault. He will be sentenced to probation, and adjudication will be withheld, meaning Brown will not be considered a convicted felon, the attorney said. Brown could have faced up to 30 years in prison if convicted of the original attempted murder charge.

Brown is accused of grabbing a handgun from a security staffer after a celebrity boxing match in Miami on May 16, 2025, and firing two shots at a man he had gotten into a fistfight with earlier, according to an arrest warrant. Zul-Qarnain Kwame Nantambu told investigators that one of the bullets grazed his neck.

Attorney insists that Brown would have prevailed at trial

"This was not an easy decision," Eiglarsh said in a statement Wednesday. "Antonio believes in his innocence. He believes strongly in his Stand Your Ground defense, and he believes he would ultimately prevail at trial. But when prosecutors put an offer on the table that transforms a potential decades-long prison sentence into a significantly reduced charge and probation, there was simply no way he could reasonably turn it down."

Florida's so-called Stand Your Ground law allows people who believe they face death or serious injury to use deadly force to defend themselves without a duty to retreat.

Richard Cooper, an attorney for Nantambu, called the plea deal fair.

"We are satisfied that justice is served. My client maintains what he said previously: that he forgives Brown and will not cooperate with law enforcement," Cooper said in an email Wednesday. "We wish Mr. Brown good health and that he grows from this event."

Nantambu's attorneys have said he'd decided to forgive Brown

In a previous statement, his attorneys said Nantambu, a devout Muslim, had made the decision to forgive Brown after "considerable reflection, prayer, and consultation with his family and counsel."

The Miami-Dade State Attorney's Office declined to comment on Wednesday, with spokesperson Ed Griffith saying the details would be "fully clarified" at next week's hearing.

Brown has said on social media that he was defending himself from an attack and that others were trying to steal jewelry from him.

Brown, 38, spent 12 years in the NFL and was an All-Pro wide receiver who last played in 2021 for Tampa Bay, including winning a Super Bowl championship with quarterback Tom Brady. He spent much of his career with Pittsburgh. For his career, Brown had 928 receptions for more than 12,000 yards and accounted for 88 total touchdowns, counting punt returns and one pass.

Brown has faced legal problems over the years

Brown was extradited in November 2025 from Dubai, where he has business interests, after an arrest warrant on the attempted murder charge was issued in June 2025.

Brown has dealt with several legal problems over the years. He previously had been accused of battery of a moving truck driver, several domestic violence charges, failure to pay child support and other incidents. During a 2021 game with Tampa Bay against the New York Jets , Brown took off his jersey, shoulder pads and gloves and ran off the field, leading to his release by the Buccaneers and effectively ending his football career.

In a separate case, Nantambu was found guilty earlier this year of a misdemeanor charge of resisting an officer after police said he disrupted Kendrick Lamar's Super Bowl halftime performance in 2025. Nantambu was among dozens of dancers on the field at Caesars Superdome in New Orleans when he ran across the field with a Sudanese flag that read "Sudan and Free Gaza." He surrendered to authorities after an arrest warrant was obtained.

articles.title: New Sam Darnold Injury Update, Timeline to Return amid Seahawks QB's 'Ramp Up' Period
articles.summary: Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald confirmed that starting quarterback Sam Darnold practiced on Wednesday, per ESPN's Adam Schefter, and would "ramp up as the practice week goes along."
articles.body:
Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald confirmed that starting quarterback Sam Darnold practiced on Wednesday, per ESPN's Adam Schefter, and would "ramp up as the practice week goes along."

It remains to be seen, however, if Darnold will play in Week 3's matchup against the Washington Commanders.

Macdonald also noted that Darnold won't take every rep with the starters on Wednesday.

Darnold suffered a glute injury on the opening drive of Seattle's Week 1 win over the New England Patriots in a Super Bowl rematch. The Seahawks have little reason to rush him back and risk another injury, however, given that Drew Lock has been superb in relief duty.

The veteran backup has thrown for 422 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions while completing 72.9 percent of his passes in parts of two games, both wins. He's also rushed for 13 yards.

"Really proud of Drew, really happy for him," Macdonald told reporters after Sunday's 31-7 win over the Arizona Cardinals. "We're on the record in how we feel about him, so he just backed that up today. That's a 12-as-one thing, everybody having each other's back. You just couldn't be happier for the guy. We just love him. All the things we said about him throughout the week, that was real. That was from the heart. Really proud of the way he played today. He did a tremendous job."

Lock showed plenty of chemistry with superstar receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who torched the Cardinals to the tune of nine receptions for 155 yards and three scores.

"We've been having a special connection for a minute now, but I'm super happy [for] the way he just came in and carried himself and carried this team," Smith-Njigba said of Lock. "He shows time and time again how good he is."

Macdonald has been resolute that once Darnold was healthy he would return to starting duties. But Lock has made it easy enough for the Seahawks to exercise patience in Darnold's recovery.

Carolina is searching for more help at running back after placing Jonathon Brooks on injured reserve due to core muscle surgery.

From 2019-23, Ekeler amassed 6,742 all-purpose yards and 58 total touchdowns while averaging 5.6 yards per touch in Los Angeles. He surpassed 400 receiving yards in each season across that span.

Ekeler eventually joined the Washington Commanders ahead of the 2024 season and entered his 2025 campaign as the team's starting running back, but suffered a torn Achilles in Week 2.

The 31-year-old missed the remainder of the season before he was fully cleared for all football activities on April 30, per Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 in Houston.

Even though the Panthers won't sign Ekeler on Wednesday, an agreement can still be reached at a later date.

Carolina is currently preparing for a Week 3 matchup with a Cleveland Browns squad that ranks No. 26 in the NFL by allowing 131.5 rush yards per game this season.

The Panthers and Browns will face off on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.

articles.title: 49ers Almost Drafted Cam Skattebo? Robert Saleh Says Kyle Shanahan 'Loved Him’
articles.summary: Titans coach Robert Saleh revealed a fascinating draft nugget regarding the 49ers and Giants running back Cam Skattebo.
articles.body: This would've been fun! Since entering the league last season, New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo has been a polarizing figure adored by fans. His downhill physicality and high-energy personality make him one of the most entertaining players to root for. Skattebo fits the identity head coach John Harbaugh wants to build with the Giants, and he’s quickly embraced the Big Apple. However, coming out of Arizona State, his path to entering the league almost looked radically different. In fact, he almost ended up right back home in Northern California, nearly drafted by the San Francisco 49ers to back up All-Pro running back Christian McCaffrey. On Wednesday afternoon, Tennessee Titans head coach Robert Saleh spoke to reporters about the team's upcoming matchup against the Giants. While praising Skattebo’s skill set and character, Saleh dropped a fascinating draft nugget. "I know going into the [2025 NFL] Draft, we were actually about to draft him in San Francisco," Saleh said. "[49ers head coach] Kyle [Shanahan] loved him, and he ended up getting taken right before we were picking. I think we ended up with C.J. West, who was a pretty good player too." Saleh was San Francisco's defensive coordinator in 2025 in what was his second stint in the role (he was also the 49ers' defensive coordinator from 2017-20); New York ultimately selected Skattebo with the No. 105 pick in that year's draft. The potential of pairing McCaffrey and Skattebo in the same backfield could've created one of the league’s premier duos, maybe even the best since the Detroit Lions drafted Jahmyr Gibbs in the first round of the 2023 NFL Draft to team up with David Montgomery? Shanahan's reputation for evaluating running backs speaks volumes about Skattebo’s potential in the league. Since being drafted by the Giants, he has hit the ground running, rushing for 527 yards and six touchdowns over his first 10 career games. After suffering a gruesome ankle injury that limited him to just eight games in 2025, Skattebo bounced back in a big way in Week 1 against the Dallas Cowboys, rushing for 81 yards and a touchdown to power the Giants to victory. Both franchises are in good hands at the position now, but Shanahan’s interest only reinforces his reputation as an elite evaluator. What could've been with a McCaffrey and Skattebo backfield is a fascinating "what-if."

articles.summary: New York Giants star pass-rusher Brian Burns is "likely to miss some time" despite not requiring surgery for an ankle injury, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter.
articles.body:
New York Giants star pass-rusher Brian Burns is "likely to miss some time" despite not requiring surgery for an ankle injury, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter .

Burns suffered the injury during New York's 28-6 defeat at the hands of the Los Angeles Rams in Week 2.

Giants head coach John Harbaugh revealed that the 28-year-old was diagnosed with a low ankle sprain after the game, per SNY's Connor Hughes .

ESPN's Jordan Raanan also reported that Burns has been wearing a boot on his foot since the loss.

The Giants were hit hard by injuries against Los Angeles, as quarterback Jaxson Dart suffered damage to his MCL, PCL and meniscus that will require season-ending surgery .

Wide receiver Malik Nabers and left tackle Andrew Thomas also suffered shoulder and groin injuries, respectively. Both players participated in Wednesday's practice, per Dan Duggan of The Athletic.

Burns' upcoming absence is a tough blow to New York's front seven, as he wrapped up a 2025 campaign in which he ranked No. 2 in the NFL with 16.5 sacks.

While he hasn't been able to take down a quarterback through two games this year, he's still made his presence felt in opposing backfields.

Burns is one of just three edge-rushers to rank within the top 10 in both pass-rush win rate and run-stop win rate, via ESPN . He's also recorded four tackles and one quarterback hit to open the 2026 season.

The Giants will rely on several players to help make up for Burns' impact moving forward including Abdul Carter and Kayvon Thibodeaux.

New York is set to face the Tennessee Titans in Week 3. The Titans have allowed five sacks through two weeks this season.

articles.title: Mike Macdonald Apologized to Sean Payton for Recent Comments, Says Video Wasn't Meant to Be Public
articles.summary: Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald told reporters on Wednesday that he reached out and apologized to Sean Payton after a video of Macdonald recounting a story about the Denver head coach was leaked Tuesday.
articles.body:
Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald told reporters on Wednesday that he reached out and apologized to Sean Payton after a video of Macdonald recounting a story about the Denver head coach was leaked Tuesday.

In the video—which appeared to be Macdonald having an off-the-record conversation with Graham Bensinger separate from the interview the head coach gave on the show—the Seattle head coach talked about pulling footage posted publicly by fans on social media that showed plays and formations the Denver Broncos were practicing during training camp ahead of a Week 1 matchup between the teams in 2024.

Macdonald said the Seahawks pulled about 100 plays that were posted online and scouted them. Seattle won the Week 1 matchup, 26-20.

Per Macdonald's story, Payton found out what happened and threatened to publicly expose the Seahawks for what he claimed was a Spygate-esque breach. Seattle and Macdonald, in turn, said they would sue Payton if he made such claims, given that they weren't filing the training camp practices and were simply looking at things that fans had posted for anybody to see.

Macdonald said Wednesday that the story was "something I didn't intend for public use" and added that he believed he was having an off-the-cuff conversation with Bensinger in the moment. He did note that he needed to take responsibility for what he said, however.

"I thought it was the most appropriate thing to just reach out to Sean and apologize to him for having that be public when it wasn't meant to," he added. "Something they have to deal with in real time that wasn't on their end, so that's really where you're like, 'Crap.' But lesson learned, honestly. I gotta be better in that moment for understanding, look, I'm responsible for what I say no matter the circumstance. Whether you're mic'd up, whether you're not, whether you have a certain type of understanding... so I fell short in that moment. It stings for me, frankly, but it's definitely something I'm going to learn from."

Macdonald said Payton was "great" when he reached out to him to apologize.

articles.title: Next man up: Ranking the NFL's backup quarterbacks for 6 teams that have had QB1 chaos
articles.summary: Backup quarterbacks have been thrust into action early in the 2026 NFL season. Some teams clearly are in better shape there than others.
articles.body:
Five plays into the 2026 NFL season, we saw the first starting quarterback go down.

The Seattle Seahawks ' Sam Darnold suffered a glute injury against the New England Patriots , and just like that, Drew Lock was leading the defending Super Bowl champs to a comeback victory on Opening Night.

It wouldn't take much longer for more starting quarterbacks to fall.

Less than 10 minutes into his Vikings debut in Week 1, Kyler Murray was knocked out with a concussion. Week 2 saw three recent first-round quarterbacks succumb to injury: Chicago 's Caleb Williams and Washington's Jayden Daniels , the first two picks of the 2024 NFL Draft, followed by the Giants' Jaxson Dart — and each injury seemingly worse than the next.

Along with the Atlanta Falcons , who were forced to start Cooper Rush the first two games ahead of either Tua Tagovailoa or Michael Penix Jr., it's fair to say that the starting-quarterback injury epidemic is already raging after two weeks. Nearly 20% of the league has been forced to play backup QBs, with almost 90% of the regular season still remaining.

Backups clearly matter. Brock Purdy missed almost half the 2025 regular season, but Mac Jones helped keep the 49ers afloat. When C.J. Stroud missed three games last season, Texans backup Davis Mills went 3-0 in his place, keeping them in the playoff race. But when Patrick Mahomes got hurt, the drop-off to Gardner Minshew — and later Chris Oladokun — was too steep for the Chiefs to survive.

Some teams, we're finding out, have protected their most important assets better than others. Here's how we'd rank the six teams that have needed to dip into their QB reserves:

6) Tua Tagovailoa/Michael Penix Jr./Cooper Rush/Jack Strand, Atlanta Falcons

Who's the starter? Who's the backup? It's often not a pretty situation when those two questions aren't followed by easy answers.

The Falcons have the toughest situation of the lot right now, even with the most theoretical options. Tagovailoa was nominally the starter until he got hurt; Penix, the logical replacement, couldn't go the first two weeks.

That left the reins to Rush, who struggled in Baltimore last season and who did little in his two starts this season in leading the Falcons to an 0-2 start. Strand, the Division-II prospect who had an encouraging preseason, replaced Rush in Week 2 and threw a pick-6 on his first NFL pass attempt.

Clearly the hope is that the often-injured Penix can step in now, having been named Atlanta's Week 3 starter, and run with the job. The Falcons have little other hope, short of (the also often-injured) Tagovailoa returning to action.

Until proven otherwise, Kevin Stefanski has the same issue in Atlanta that he had in Cleveland : quarterback uncertainty.

With Jaxson Dart now ruled out for the season , the Giants are in a really tough spot, with no young quarterback to prepare in the wings. Winston has a wealth of experience, with 89 career starts, but as Monday's replacement performance showed, his play can be a wild experience.

Winston struggled against the Rams and has been a turnover machine in his career, with 141 of them (114 INTs, 27 lost fumbles) in 109 career outings. He's had a five-pick game and a three-fumble game. Winston also has five career 400-yard games and two five-TD, no-INT performances. You really never know what you're going to get any given week.

Head coach John Harbaugh has to find another option in case he gets too much bad Winston, with only Jake Haener currently on the practice squad. Some have floated a J.J. McCarthy trade to the Giants, but would that throw only more gas on the fire?

4) Tyson Bagent/Case Keenum, Chicago Bears

This pairing could arguably be higher on the list, but Bagent's concussion (which might have come on the final play Sunday) could keep him out of Monday night's game against the Philadelphia Eagles , which would give Keenum his first start — and his first regular-season action — since 2023.

Bagent has barely seen the field since Caleb Williams was drafted, but he started four games in 2023 and replaced Williams for the final two drives Sunday. His body of work is incomplete, but Bagent possesses intriguing skills and it wouldn't be shocking if he led a team at starter level for a stretch.

It's unclear how long Williams will be out, but for the first time since he came to Chicago, the Bears will have to lean on his replacements.

3) Drew Lock/ Jalen Milroe , Seattle Seahawks

Lock came in cold in Week 1 and did just enough to help the Seahawks win, settling down after a few shaky patches. Then he came out guns blazing in Week 2, throwing for three TDs. Would you believe that Lock leads the NFL in passer rating through two games? He entered the season completing fewer than 60% of his career passes but is sitting at 72.7% in 2026.

If Lock, who turns 30 in November, can continue to fill in ably for the injured Darnold, it's not a stretch to think he could follow the Geno Smith post-30 path of earning his way back into a starting lineup, perhaps as a bridge option for a team that drafts a higher-round QB next spring. It appears that Lock has worked out some of the recklessness in his game and is becoming more dependable.

Milroe remains a curiosity with strong physical skills, but he's still virtually unknown. His best shot might be to continue working behind the scenes and vie for Lock's QB2 spot next season.

2) Carson Wentz /J.J. McCarthy, Minnesota Vikings

Wentz might be known in some circles as a bust, or as the guy whose team went on to win a Super Bowl after he got hurt. Even still, he's carved out a career for himself as an able QB2, willing and ready to jump into the fire. He did so early against the Packers when Kyler Murray got hurt, leading the Vikings to a 12-point comeback in the game's final 20 minutes. Then Wentz turned in a solid, turnover-free effort in his Week 2 start against the Bears, leading Minnesota to a shocking 9-3 win and a 2-0 start to the season.

Not bad for a guy who wasn't even part of the Vikings' starting derby in camp. His outing vs. the Bears marked 11 straight seasons with at least one start for Wentz. He'll take a seat again with Murray expected to start in Week 3, but Wentz's contributions can't be forgotten.

McCarthy, who lost the starting battle to Murray, remains an enigma. He's under contract through 2027 with a 2028 option, but the path back to being relevant for this team appears longer and more windy now.

1) Marcus Mariota /Athan Kaliakmanis, Washington Commanders

Mariota is in some ways the gold standard of backup quarterbacks, along with the 49ers' Jones. With 82 career starts, Mariota has more experience than many current starters. He stepped in ably for Jayden Daniels in Sunday's loss to the Cowboys, looking sharp, and was competitive during Daniels' two missed stints last season.

With Daniels expected to miss 4-6 weeks with his latest left elbow injury, Mariota will be thrust back onto the saddle as he approaches his 33rd birthday. The biggest benefit is that he can run the same offense Daniels did, with little tweaking necessary.

The rookie Kaliakmanis had a strong preseason, receiving extra reps when Mariota's knee injury flared up and impressing the team with his arm talent and moxie.

Jameis Winston (Jaxson Dart out for season, knee)

Marcus Mariota (Jayden Daniels out, elbow)

Tyson Bagent/Case Keenum (Caleb Williams out, hamstring)

Tua Tagovailoa/ Cooper Rush / Jack Strand

Drew Lock (Sam Darnold missed Week 2 , glute)

articles.title: Derek Carr Responds to Photo of Giants Uniform Edit amid Comeback Speculation After Dart Injury
articles.summary: Former NFL quarterback Derek Carr reacted to speculation that he could come back and join the New York Giants following Jaxson Dart's knee injury.
articles.body:
Former NFL quarterback Derek Carr reacted to speculation that he could come back and join the New York Giants following Jaxson Dart's knee injury.

Carr responded to an edit of himself in a Giants uniform on X, explaining that he's currently focused on searching for a crew to join in NBA 2K27.

The 35-year-old previously started 169 games throughout his 11 seasons in the NFL before announcing his retirement in May 2025.

Dart is set to undergo season-ending surgery after suffering damage to his MCL, PCL and meniscus during New York's 28-6 defeat at the hands of the Los Angeles Rams on Monday.

Backup Jameis Winston will replace Dart under center, but New York is also looking to add an external option after Winston completed just 40.7 percent of his throws for 111 yards and one interception against Los Angeles.

Giants head coach John Harbaugh confirmed that the team will be bringing in another quarterback, per Dan Duggan of The Athletic.

"All options are open," Harbaugh told reporters on Wednesday.

While Carr last played in the NFL during the 2024 season and retired following a shoulder injury , he hasn't completely shut the door on a comeback.

"I never say never," Carr said during a July appearance on Good Morning Football . "It would take a special situation. There were multiple teams that reached out to me this offseason. I won't say who or how, but they reached out and were gauging my interest on what I wanted to do. They were good, solid football teams."

The four-time Pro Bowler appeared in 10 games during his final year on the New Orleans Saints, completing 67.7 percent of his passes for 2,145 yards and 15 touchdowns while getting picked off five times.

Although the Giants are searching for another signal-caller, it doesn't seem as though Carr is a legitimate possibility.

articles.title: Puka Nacua Injury Update, Rams HC Provides Latest on Star WR After Missing Week 2
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams might be without their star receiver for another week.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams might be without their star receiver for another week.

Rams head coach Sean McVay offered an update on Puka Nacua after he missed Week 2, saying that he does not have a hernia, but the team is being cautious with his return.

"Usually time is the best thing that allows that thing to heal," McVay told reporters . "And then once you get to a certain point, then I think you feel pretty good moving forward."

Nacua landed on the injury report with a hip injury on Friday and McVay told reporters ahead of Monday's game against the New York Giants that he was dealing with "a little bit of soreness" in his groin and that he "didn't feel totally like himself" in practice.

McVay then told reporters on Tuesday that he was "hopeful" Nacua would be on the field in Week 3 but didn't say with certainty that he'd be available.

Nacua is coming off the best season of his career in which he recorded 129 receptions for 1,715 yards and 10 touchdowns, earning First Team All-Pro honors and a third-place finish in the NFL Offensive Player of the Year voting.

The Rams' offense struggled in their season-opening loss in Melbourne against the San Francisco 49ers, but Nacua still managed to collect five catches for 74 yards.

Having their WR1 back on the field for Sunday's matchup against the Denver Broncos would be a major boost for the Rams, but they showed on Monday that they can still get the offense going without him.

In a 28-6 win over the Giants, Davante Adams led the offense with eight receptions for 195 yards and two touchdowns. Reigning MVP Matthew Stafford also returned to form, recording 327 passing yards and four touchdowns.

Going up against Denver's defense will be much more challenging than the one Los Angeles faced on Monday, but if the Rams can get close to matching Monday's success, they should be able to get a win even if Nacua is sidelined.

articles.title: Mel Kiper Jr. Reveals His Top-3 QB's, WR's in 2027 NFL Draft Amid Arch Manning, Jeremiah Smith Buzz
articles.summary: ESPN NFL draft analyst Mel Kiper Jr. ranked his top-three 2027 draft prospects at five different positions (quarterback, wide receiver, edge-rusher, cornerbacks, offensive tackle) on the latest edition of First Draft.
articles.body:
ESPN NFL draft analyst Mel Kiper Jr. ranked his top-three 2027 draft prospects at five different positions (quarterback, wide receiver, edge-rusher, cornerbacks, offensive tackle) on the latest edition of First Draft .

A few big names (Texas quarterback Arch Manning and Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith) made the lists, which you can see below. Of note, Kiper had two quarterback lists: his current top-three and his projected top-three.

ESPN's Field Yates also listed his top three at each position. Notes on his rankings are below.

Cam Coleman, Texas (Yates Had Becker No. 2, Coleman No. 3)

Yhonzae Pierre and Devon Thompkins, Alabama

Smith's No. 1 spot on the wideout list is no surprise. In 32 games over two-plus seasons, Smith has caught 184 passes for 2,958 yards and 30 touchdowns. In three games this season, the junior has caught 21 passes for 400 yards and three scores.

The B/R NFL Scouting Department lists Smith as the top overall prospect in the 2027 draft with an eye-popping grade of 9.8 out of 10.

It wouldn't be a surprise to see Smith go No. 1 overall at this point. The latest B/R NFL mock draft has Smith at the top to the Miami Dolphins.

There's an open race to be QB1 right now. Manning could be the pick, but it's anyone's guess who will be the first off the board in April. Manning's passing stats haven't popped off the screen (61.5 percent completion rate, 661 yards, 6.9 yards per attempt, seven touchdowns, two interceptions).

However, he currently leads the nation's No. 1 team and led the Longhorns to a dramatic 20-point comeback win over OSU, 24-23. Manning will get plenty of chances to impress scouts under bright lights this year.

The same goes for a host of other quarterbacks and top prospects heading into a highly anticipated draft that could threaten the record for most signal-callers taken in Round 1 (six in 1983 and 2024).

articles.title: Like father, like son: Dez Bryant Jr. isn't the only Cowboys legacy starring at Southlake Carroll
articles.summary: The sons of Bryant and DeMarcus Ware are starting a legacy of their own with the eight-time state champion Carroll.
articles.body:
SOUTHLAKE — On Southlake Carroll 's opening drive of the game last Thursday against Keller Central , Dez Bryant Jr. took a handoff, found a hole up the middle, had his facemask grabbed for an instant by a defender as he was racing by and continued unimpeded into the end zone for a 14-yard touchdown.

After crossing the goal line for the first touchdown of his Carroll career, Bryant Jr. made an X sign with his arms. The scene repeated itself later in the first quarter on a 15-yard run: another touchdown and another X sign.

He was paying homage to his father, former Cowboy and three-time Pro Bowl wide receiver Dez Bryant , who made the X his trademark celebration each time he scored one of his 75 NFL touchdowns. Bryant Jr., a junior wide receiver/running back, was also introducing another member of the family who could be a star on the football field.

"It was a tribute to him, but also just a start to my own legacy," Bryant Jr. said. "I'm carrying on where he left off, but in my own fashion."

As always, Dad was there to witness it. He's a regular at Carroll games and practices.

"It's an honor," the elder Bryant said. "He's been watching Dad do that all his life, so just to see him do that just showed Dad a little bit of love. It was kind of emotional, but it was great to see."

Bryant Jr. isn't the only son of a former professional athlete who is playing for eight-time state champion Carroll. Sophomore linebacker DeMarcus Ware Jr.'s dad was a Hall of Fame linebacker and a nine-time Pro Bowler who had 138.5 sacks during his 12-year NFL career with the Cowboys and Broncos . Freshman Jason Maxiell II's father is a former Carrollton Newman Smith star who averaged 5.6 points and 4.2 rebounds during a 10-season NBA career.

"I got to watch him [play in the NFL] a little bit," Ware Jr. said. "I saw him play in the Super Bowl. That was a pretty unique experience. He helps me with a lot of stuff, just how to do things on and off the field. Like how I play on the field, keeping that same integrity off the field, keeping my grades up, making sure my teammates are keeping it together in class."

Combined with Bryant Jr., the three players have more than 25 college offers.

"I think it's awesome," Carroll coach Lee Munn said. "They are all three pretty intrinsically motivated to be really good. All three of their dads have played at a really high level, so they have that internal belief that they are capable."

Southlake, a thriving suburb of just over 31,000 residents about 25 miles west of Dallas , has become home for several former Cowboys players.

Russell Maryland, a Pro Bowl defensive tackle for the Cowboys who won three Super Bowls, saw his son RJ Maryland become a four-star tight end at Carroll and go on to play at SMU. Christian Glenn, son of the late Cowboys wide receiver Terry Glenn, was a running back on Carroll's state runner-up team in 2024 and is now at the University of Mount Union.

Ware Jr. grew up in Southlake, while Bryant Jr. transferred to Carroll last year after previously attending Colleyville Heritage.

"I've always lived in this area," Bryant Jr.'s dad said. "I had a home here and mom had a home in Colleyville. One of my dreams was to get him here. Carroll is a great program for development, especially if you've got some talent. I think they are one of the top high schools that can get your kid prepared for college ball."

Munn doesn't feel pressured having former pro athletes watching how he coaches their sons, he said, and none of the three came into the program feeling entitled or expecting to start just because of who their fathers are. Munn said he has a good relationship with Bryant and gladly listens to any advice he offers.

Carroll, a Class 6A Division II state semifinalist last season, is 2-2 after beating Keller Central 35-17 last week in its District 4-6A opener. Bryant Jr. ran for 77 yards and two touchdowns on 14 carries after being used more as a running back than wide receiver, his normal position.

Maxiell II, a two-sport athlete who also plays basketball and lists football offers from Texas, Texas A&M, SMU, Baylor and Texas State, said he thinks Carroll can win its first state title since 2011, even though the team has already matched its loss total for the last two years combined.

"I think we're capable of making state and winning state and going undefeated from now on," he said.

Ware Jr. and Bryant Jr. said watching film of, and with, their fathers is a regular occurrence.

"It's pretty much every day after practice, just a quick 30-minute session to critique a few things," Ware Jr. said.

Bryant Jr. said he also watches video of NFL stars Justin Jefferson , Ja'Marr Chase and Zay Flowers and of college standouts Malachi Toney and Jeremiah Smith to hone his skills.

"It's a great thing," Bryant Jr. said of having a dad who played in the NFL. "I get to learn from somebody who has done it at the highest level, and I get to implement that into my game, as in how I need to work, how I need to prepare, how to watch film. Watching film isn't just clicking through plays. It's deeply analyzing each player's movement."

Besides throwing up the X after he scored, Bryant Jr. had another moment this season in which he looked like his dad. In a season-opening win over Jenks (Okla.), he caught an 18-yard pass and appeared to have scored before being ruled down at the 1-yard line. As he lay there, with the ball stretched toward the goal line, he resembled the famous photo of his father from a Cowboys playoff loss to the Packers in January 2015, when he had a play near the goal line first ruled a catch before being overturned to one of the most legendary incompletions in NFL history.

But that's not what Bryant Jr. remembers about his play. He and his father just talked about Bryant Jr.'s release as he was beginning his route and what he could have done differently.

Bryant Jr. has 14 offers, including one from his father's alma mater, Oklahoma State. The elder Bryant isn't trying to sway his son on where to go.

"I am going to take him down [to visit], but everything is up to him," he said. "It's his life. I'm his pops, and I'm just here to support him."

Even though he was a superstar for "America's Team," Bryant said he doesn't talk about his NFL career with his son that often. Ware Jr., who has offers from Colorado, Colorado State, UTEP, UT-San Antonio, SMU and Baylor, said his father is the same way.

"He got to witness it, so I don't talk to him much," Bryant said of his career. "Now if he asks me a question, I give him my best advice or my best opinion, but other than that I sit behind him. I let him live his life, and whatever he needs, I'm just there."

That Bryant is at games and practices, watching his son intently, is something Bryant Jr. embraces. Especially the feedback, whether it's positive or negative.

"It's like having someone in your ear all the time, but in a positive way," Bryant Jr. said. "You've got to do this, you've got to do that. But it's really how you take it. You can either crumble and fold or you can take it in a positive way and add it to your game. I feel like that's what I've been doing so far."

articles.title: Joe Burrow defends Orlando Brown Jr. amid early-season struggles
articles.summary: Has his LT’s back.
articles.body:
Cincinnati Bengals franchise quarterback Joe Burrow entered Week 2's victory over the Houston Texans with back soreness. While he was questionable to play, he ultimately finished the game without much issue, despite taking a good amount of hits from Houston's talented defensive front.

Many of those hits appeared to come from the left side of the offensive line, leading to criticism of left tackle Orlando Brown Jr. Brown spent a lot of time in one-on-one matchups with Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter , who got in the backfield quite a bit.

Brown did better in Week 1, though he still allowed two QB hits on Burrow. The 30-year-old Brown now leads the Bengals in allowed sacks (three), QB hits (three), and total pressures (six).

Despite fan and media criticism, Burrow spoke to the media Wednesday and stood up for Brown, stating that all of the hits weren't his fault.

"I think Orlando was pretty good. There were a couple sacks that weren't in his control at the end of the day. There's a lot of different things that go into pass protection that's not just on the offensive line, and that's what you don't see in the media," Burrow said.

Burrow is correct. On TV, we just see a player hit the quarterback, see who lined up in front of him, and then blame that player, but there truly is a lot more that goes into a sack or quarterback pressure than the naked eye sees on game day.

"There's very intricate details of past protection, and guys expecting help here. Guys expecting help from a different spot," Burrow said. "A lot of different things that go into it that we would never explain to you guys, and then it's left up to interpretation, and that's that's how football works, and that's the o-ine position at the end of the day.

"That is a thankless job from the exterior, so you try to pump those guys up as much as you can in the building. But I really think they were pretty good on Sunday."

While it may not have been his best day, Burrow doesn't sound like he holds any ill will toward his left tackle. Instead, Burrow is publicly backing Brown ahead of a road divisional matchup with the Pittsburgh Steelers , who also have a dangerous pass rush.

articles.title: Fernando Mendoza Follows 'True Passion' with New Video Series Amid NFL Rookie Season with Raiders
articles.summary: Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza is launching a fiscal responsibility series called "Finance with Fernando," which the rookie described as a "practical guide for Gen Z to make the most of their money."
articles.body:
Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza is launching a fiscal responsibility series called "Finance with Fernando," which the rookie described as a "practical guide for Gen Z to make the most of their money."

The series is through U.S. Bank, which launched a brand campaign on Aug. 31 with Mendoza, a.k.a. the "Chief Financial Playmaker."

"The campaign brings Mendoza's passion for football and finance together to help make money conversations more approachable for younger audiences, NFL fans and U.S. Bank clients," a press release read.

"The new work is part of the bank's broader brand platform, 'The Power of Us,' and builds on the company's role as an Official Bank and Wealth Management Sponsor of the NFL. Acknowledging that Gen Z faces real financial stress, Mendoza as Chief Financial Playmaker helps to make banking feel like one less thing to worry about – one cozy conversation at a time."

Mendoza is a good source. Last year, the Heisman Trophy winner (and No. 1 overall pick in April's NFL draft) graduated with a Bachelor of Science in Business Administration from Cal's Haas School of Business.

Mendoza played football at Cal before transferring to Indiana before the 2025 season, where he took MBA courses at the Kelley School of Business.

When he wasn't in the classroom, Mendoza was guiding the Hoosiers to a 16-0 record and their first-ever national championship.

Now he's in the NFL on a fully guaranteed $57.3 million deal . One can safely assume Mendoza will know how to manage that money well.

In the meantime, he's waiting in the wings as the Raiders' backup quarterback while veteran Kirk Cousins starts and leads the squad on a promising 2-0 start. Mendoza will be the franchise signal-caller someday, but in his downtime, he's hoping to teach people a thing or two about fiscal responsibility.

articles.title: NFL: New York Giants Quarterback Jaxson Dart ruled out for the 2026 season due to knee injury
articles.summary: Jaxson Dart suffered a knee injury in the New York Giants game on Monday against the Los Angeles Rams and will miss the remainder of the 2026 season
articles.body:
Dart was injured on the first drive on Monday night against the Los Angeles Rams when his left leg bent awkwardly as he was hit by two defenders.

After initially saying it was in the neighborhood of a medial collateral ligament injury, coach John Harbaugh said on Tuesday the evaluation process for Dart was still ongoing.

An MRI revealed medial collateral ligament, posterior cruciate ligament and meniscus damage, according to a report by NFL Network .

Harbaugh was due to address reporters after practice later on Wednesday.

Losing the 23-year-old to a long-term injury is a significant blow in Harbaugh's first season in charge, which began with a victory against Dallas at home in Week 1.

Jameis Winston will take over the starting role, beginning Sunday against Tennessee.

The Giants' next five opponents have a combined 2-8 record. Winston is 3-9 in 12 NFL starts since 2024.

Winston and Jake Haener, who is on the practice squad, were the only QBs at practice during the portion open to reporters.

Haener, who played in eight games and started one for New Orleans two seasons ago, joined midway through training camp and stuck around over journeyman Brandon Allen.

Edge rusher Brian Burns, who sprained his left ankle late in the Rams game, was not on the field.

No 1 receiver Malik Nabers, who popped his shoulder back into place and returned Monday night, and starting left tackle Andrew Thomas, who limped off with a groin injury, were participating in the unpadded session.
